user.title: Connect to the Vördr hub
user.description: Home Assistant becomes a client of the hub. It creates its own key; the hub's operator admits it.

data_description.url: WebSocket address of the hub, e.g. wss://hub.example:8443/v1/ha
data_description.name: How this Home Assistant appears at the hub: lower case letters, digits, dot and hyphen
data_description.ca_pem: Only if the hub's certificate comes from an own CA; then only this CA is trusted

progress.approval:
Waiting for the hub's operator. Compare the fingerprint and admit this client on the hub:

`{command}`

Fingerprint: `{fingerprint}`

You may close this dialog: Home Assistant keeps this key for the hub and the client name, and adding the integration again with the same name continues this request.

error.invalid_name: Use lower case letters, digits, dot and hyphen (at most 63 characters).
error.probe_dns: The hub's name does not resolve.
error.probe_connect: No connection to the hub (address, port, firewall, hub not running).
error.probe_tls: The hub's certificate is not trusted (chain, name or CA certificate).
error.probe_websocket: TLS works, but there is no Vördr endpoint at this path.
error.probe_challenge: The other side answers, but it is no Vördr hub speaking this protocol.

abort.already_configured: This hub is already set up.
abort.unreachable: The hub could not be reached while waiting for approval.
abort.approval_timeout: No decision within an hour. Add the integration again with the same client name: Home Assistant kept its key, so it continues the request that the hub keeps.
abort.rejected_key_mismatch: The hub knows the client name {name} with another key. This Home Assistant's fingerprint is {fingerprint}; `vordr-hub clients` shows the one the hub knows. If the name belongs to no other Home Assistant, forget it on the hub (`vordr-hub forget-client {name}`) and add the integration again; otherwise choose another name.
abort.rejected_too_many_pending: Too many clients are waiting for approval at the hub.
abort.rejected_rejected: The operator rejected this client at the hub.
abort.rejected_protocol_mismatch: The hub speaks another protocol version than this integration; update one of them.
abort.rejected_bad_hello: The hub did not accept the login (invalid name or signature).

user.title: Add a host
user.description:
Installs the Vördr agent on a new host. For Linux with systemd and apt only (Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS). Home Assistant reaches the host once over SSH, has it fetch the signed agent release from the hub, checks size and SHA-256 against the manifest signed with your operator key, and runs `vordr-agent install`. Nothing of the SSH access is stored: no password, no key, no host key; nor is the host stored here: the hub keeps the list of hosts. Afterwards the host waits for approval at the hub, like any new host; where the hub lets this Home Assistant approve hosts (`ha_approves_hosts` in hub.yaml, role admin), this dialog approves it right after the install.

The hub hands out the agent release only to a client with role admin. If this Home Assistant has another role, at the hub: `vordr-hub client-role {client} --role admin`.

Next you check the host key, before you enter a password.

data_description.host: Name or address of the new host, as Home Assistant reaches it (IPv6 without brackets).
data_description.username: root, or a user that may use sudo.
data_description.node: Its name at the hub. Empty: the host's own name in lower case.

host_key.title: Check the host key
host_key.description:
{host}:{port} presents this host key ({algorithm}):

`{fingerprint}`

Compare it with the host's own, on its console: `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/{key_file}`. Go on only if they are the same: otherwise someone may sit between Home Assistant and the host. The login accepts only this key; nothing is written to a known_hosts file.

menu_options.login: They are the same: log in

login.title: Log in
login.description: Log in as {username} on {host}: with a password or a private key. If {username} is not root, sudo needs its password unless it asks for none; empty, the login password is used. All of it serves this install only: Home Assistant holds it in memory until the install ends and stores it nowhere. If you can, use a key or a password made for this purpose.

data_description.password: Of the user, for the SSH login.
data_description.ssh_key: Paste the whole key (OpenSSH or PEM), from its first to its last line.
data_description.ssh_key_passphrase: Only for a key with a passphrase.
data_description.sudo_password: Empty: the login password, or none if sudo asks for none.

progress.install: Installing the agent on {host}: the signed release from the hub, checked against your operator key; downloaded on the host, its size and SHA-256 compared; then `vordr-agent install`. Where the hub lets this Home Assistant approve hosts, up to a minute more until the hub lists the new host, which is then approved. This may take a few minutes. Closing this dialog stops waiting for the result; the host finishes or stops on its own and removes its temporary folder.

error.invalid_host: A host name or an IP address (IPv6 without brackets).
error.invalid_username: A user name: letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, at most 32.
error.invalid_node: A node name as the hub takes it: lower case letters, digits, dot and hyphen, at most 63.
error.credentials_missing: A password or a private key.
error.ssh_key_invalid: This private key cannot be read: paste all of it, from its first to its last line; for a key with a passphrase, enter the passphrase.
error.ssh_unreachable: The host is not reachable: check the name, the address and the port.
error.ssh_timeout: The host does not answer in time.
error.ssh_failed: The other side does not speak SSH as expected, or offers no host key type the install accepts (ED25519, ECDSA, RSA with SHA-2).
error.ssh_no_host_key: The host presented no host key.
error.ssh_auth_failed: The login was refused: user, password or key wrong, or the host does not allow this way of logging in.
error.ssh_lost: The connection to the host ended. Nothing was changed.
error.sudo_failed: sudo refused: the password is wrong, or the user may not use sudo.
error.sudo_needs_password: sudo asks for a password: enter it here (or log in with a password).

abort.entry_not_loaded: The integration is not running: reload it, then try again.
abort.install_needs_operator_key: First enter the operator key: Configure → Operator keys, at the integration's entry. Home Assistant checks the agent release against it before anything runs on the host, and never takes a key from the hub: otherwise a hub that was taken over could hand out a binary of its own.
abort.install_needs_ssh_library: The SSH library "Add host" needs (`asyncssh`) is not installed; Home Assistant installs it with the integration: restart Home Assistant, or set the agent up on the host by hand with `vordr-agent install` (deploy/README.md). Everything else of the integration works without it.
abort.hub_not_connected: Home Assistant is not connected to the hub or not approved there; the install needs the hub for the signed agent release.
abort.hub_without_download: This hub does not hand out the agent release for a new host yet: update the hub, then try again.
abort.install_cancelled: The dialog was closed while logging in: the connection to the host is closed, nothing was asked of the hub and nothing was changed on the host.
abort.host_output_too_long: The host printed more than Home Assistant reads from it, so Home Assistant stopped reading and closed the connection. The install's commands print a few lines: check the host. If this happened during the install, its state is unknown: on the host, `systemctl status vordr-agent` and `vordr-agent identity` tell.
abort.host_key_rejected: Stopped: the host key of {host} was not confirmed, and nothing was sent to the host. If the keys differ, find out why before you log in there.
abort.ssh_host_key_changed: Stopped: {host} now presents another host key than the one you confirmed. Nothing secret was sent. Someone may sit between Home Assistant and the host: find out why.
abort.probe_failed: The host does not answer as a Linux shell does. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.not_linux: The host runs `{os}`, not Linux. Installing from Home Assistant is for Linux with systemd and apt; on Windows, `vordr-agent install-service` sets the agent up. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.unknown_arch: There is no agent build for the processor `{machine}` (there are builds for x86_64, aarch64 and armv7). Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.no_systemd: systemd does not run on this host: the agent runs as its service. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.no_apt: There is no apt-get on this host: the agent knows the apt source only (Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS). Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.no_download_tool: Neither curl nor wget is on this host: install one of them, then try again. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.missing_tools: Missing on the host: {tools}. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.no_sudo: The user is not root, and there is no sudo: log in as root, or install sudo. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.role_forbids: The hub hands out the agent release only to a client with role admin. At the hub: `vordr-hub client-role {client} --role admin`, then try again. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.client_not_approved: The hub no longer counts this Home Assistant as approved. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.no_release: The hub has no agent release: sign one with `vordr-release` and put it on the hub. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.no_binary_for_platform: The agent release has no build for this host's processor. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.release_incomplete: A binary of the agent release is missing on the hub or has another size: put the release on the hub again. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.too_many_downloads: The hub has handed out as many downloads as it allows for now: try again in 15 minutes. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.bad_request: The hub did not take the request. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.hub_refused: The hub refused with `{code}`. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.no_answer: The hub did not answer in time. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.manifest_invalid: The hub's answer holds no readable manifest. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.manifest_signature_invalid: The agent release is not signed with your operator key, so it is not run. Compare the key under "Operator keys" with `vordr-release public-key`; if it is right, the hub hands out a release you did not sign. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.release_too_old: The hub hands out agent release {version}, older than release {newest}, which an earlier install from Home Assistant took. Every release you signed stays valid, so an older one is not taken again: a hub that was taken over could hand out an old release with a known weakness. Publish the current release at the hub (`vordr-release`); going back means publishing the old code under a new version. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.download_invalid: The hub's answer has no valid download for this host. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.bad_input: The host did not receive what Home Assistant sent (with sudo: did it read more than its password?). Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.temp_failed: There is no private temporary folder on the host (mktemp). Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.temp_noexec: Nothing may run from the host's temporary folder (mounted noexec?): set the agent up on the host by hand with `vordr-agent install` (deploy/README.md). Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.ca_failed: The hub's CA certificate could not be put on the host. Nothing was installed.
abort.ca_differs: `{ca_path}` is on the host already and differs from this hub's CA certificate: compare them there. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.download_failed: The host could not download the agent from the hub (`{tool}`, exit {exit}): does it reach the hub at the address Home Assistant uses? Nothing was installed.
abort.download_unreachable: The host gets no connection to the hub at `{hub}` (`{tool}`, exit {exit}): the hub's name does not resolve there, or a firewall at the hub or between the two blocks this host. Allow it there and try again. Nothing was installed.
abort.download_refused: The hub refused the download (HTTP {http}, `{reason}`): try again. Nothing was installed.
abort.download_too_large: The hub sent more than the signed size of the agent (`{tool}`): the host stopped the download at that size and deleted it. Nothing was installed.
abort.size_mismatch: The downloaded agent does not have the size the signed manifest names: it was not run and is deleted. Nothing was installed.
abort.hash_mismatch: The downloaded agent does not match the SHA-256 the signed manifest names: it was not run and is deleted. Nothing was installed.
abort.ssh_lost: The connection to the host ended during the install. Its state is unknown: on the host, `systemctl status vordr-agent` and `vordr-agent identity` tell.
abort.ssh_timeout: The install did not end in time. Its state is unknown: on the host, `systemctl status vordr-agent` and `vordr-agent identity` tell.
abort.install_no_result: The install on the host gave no result Home Assistant can read. Its state is unknown: on the host, `systemctl status vordr-agent` and `vordr-agent identity` tell.
abort.agent_installed:
The agent {version} is installed on `{node}` and waits for approval at the hub. Its fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

As soon as the hub lists the host, Home Assistant shows a repair with the command that approves it: compare the fingerprint there with this one, then run the command at the hub, or, where the hub lets this Home Assistant approve hosts, fix the repair here. Once approved, the host shows as a device of this integration. Nothing of the SSH access was stored, and the host is not stored here either: the hub keeps the list of hosts.
abort.agent_installed_approved:
The agent {version} is installed on `{node}` and approved at the hub. Its fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

Home Assistant read it over the SSH connection whose host key you confirmed, and the hub listed the new host with exactly this fingerprint. The host shows as a device of this integration shortly. Nothing of the SSH access was stored, and the host is not stored here either: the hub keeps the list of hosts.
abort.agent_installed_not_approved:
The agent {version} is installed on `{node}` and waits for approval at the hub; the hub did not approve it from here (`{code}`). Its fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

As soon as the hub lists the host, Home Assistant shows a repair with the command that approves it: compare the fingerprint there with this one, then run the command at the hub, or, where the hub lets this Home Assistant approve hosts, fix the repair here. Once approved, the host shows as a device of this integration. Nothing of the SSH access was stored, and the host is not stored here either: the hub keeps the list of hosts.
abort.agent_config_invalid: `vordr-agent install` refused: the agent.yaml for these values has issues; run it on the host to see them. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.agent_config_differs: `vordr-agent install` refused: there is an /etc/vordr/agent.yaml on the host already, and it differs. Compare it there; to replace it, run `vordr-agent install` on the host with `--replace-config` and your reason. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.agent_hub_unreachable: `vordr-agent install` refused: the host does not reach the hub at `{hub}` (stage `{stage}`). Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.agent_installer_refused: `vordr-agent install` refused: its installer found something it does not change by itself, e.g. a proxy instance whose policy the new binary does not take; run it on the host to see it. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.agent_prepare_failed: `vordr-agent install` could not prepare the install (its binary, bash or its private folder). Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.agent_refused: `vordr-agent install` refused with `{code}`. Nothing was changed on the host.
abort.agent_install_failed: The install failed after it had started to change the host. Check there: `systemctl status vordr-agent`, `journalctl -u vordr-agent`.
abort.agent_identity_unreadable: The agent is installed and started, but its fingerprint could not be read: on the host, `vordr-agent identity` shows it.
abort.agent_failed: `vordr-agent install` failed with `{code}` after it had started to change the host. Check there: `systemctl status vordr-agent`.
abort.agent_no_result: The agent from the hub gave no result Home Assistant can read (exit {exit}). Is the release on the hub older than `vordr-agent install`? Its state is unknown: on the host, `systemctl status vordr-agent` and `vordr-agent identity` tell.

ha_updates.title: Home Assistant updates
ha_updates.description: Which of Home Assistant's own updates (Core, OS, apps, HACS, ESPHome, device firmware) Vördr's rules let through, and when. Nothing chosen, nothing allowed. Vördr installs what they let through only once "Install automatically" is on: one update at a time, inside the window, Core, OS and Supervisor last, each with a backup before it, except device firmware and the radio adapter, which a backup of Home Assistant cannot undo. Until then the sensor "Updates ready" of the device "Vördr Home Assistant" only shows what it would do. Never by Vördr: its own entities, an update that installs itself, a version skipped in Home Assistant, and a new major version (that stays by hand). Device firmware and the radio adapter wait at least {firmware_days} days, or the minimum age if that is longer. A newer release of a version line Vördr has seen before (the same first two numbers, such as 2026.11.2 after 2026.11.1) counts its age from when Vördr first saw the line, but waits at least {patch_days} days itself, or the minimum age if that is shorter.

data_description.kinds: Every update entity of a chosen kind, told by its integration and its device. The firmware of the radio adapter is a kind of its own.
data_description.entities: Update entities allowed besides the chosen kinds.
data_description.days: The window belongs to the day it starts on. Needed as soon as anything is allowed.
data_description.start: In Home Assistant's time zone. If the start is after the end, the window runs past midnight.
data_description.end: From the end on, nothing new would start.
data_description.min_age_days: 1 to 90 days, counted from when Vördr first saw the version: Home Assistant gives no release date.
data_description.auto_install: Off: Vördr only plans. On: Vördr installs what is ready, one at a time, inside the window, with a backup before it (the entity's own, else Home Assistant's automatic backup, no older than 26 hours; none for device firmware and the radio adapter, which a backup of Home Assistant cannot roll back). The switch "Pause Home Assistant updates" holds it at any time. Only one Vördr entry may install.

ai_explanations.title: AI explanations of failed runs
ai_explanations.description: Optional, off while no entity is chosen. When a run on a host fails, Vördr asks the AI Task entity chosen here once for a short explanation in Home Assistant's language, a likely cause and next steps from fixed lists, and a quote from the run's log excerpt as evidence. Sent to the entity's provider: the result code, the action, the package names and the end of the log excerpt. The host names Vördr knows, IP addresses, the hub's address and the server in any address are replaced by placeholders first; the other words of the excerpt go as they are. The answer is advice only: the event `vordr_ai_explanation` and the host's sensor "Last run" show it, and it never changes windows, minimum ages, scopes, buttons or repairs. An answer whose quote is not part of what was sent counts as unverified, and nothing of it is shown.

data.data_ack: Package names and log excerpts of failed runs may go to this entity's provider

data_description.entity_id: An AI Task entity that can generate data, e.g. of a local model or of a cloud service. Empty: off.
data_description.data_ack: Needed with an entity. The provider may be a cloud service, also behind an integration for local models: check where the entity sends its data.

operator_keys.title: Operator keys
operator_keys.description: The public keys the agent release must be signed with (base64, as `vordr-release public-key` prints them). Before anything reaches a new host, Home Assistant checks the release the hub hands out against these keys; it never takes a key from the hub. The new host gets them for its self-update. Public keys, no secret. Empty: "Add host" cannot install the agent.

data_description.operator_key: Ed25519 public key in base64, as `vordr-release public-key` prints it.
data_description.backup_operator_key: Optional: the key that takes over if the first one is lost. A release signed with either is accepted.

error.window_empty: Start and end are equal: the window would have no length.
error.window_needs_days: Choose at least one day: otherwise the window never opens, and nothing allowed would ever be installed.
error.min_age_days: A whole number of days from 1 to 90.
error.auto_install_other_entry: Another Vördr entry already installs Home Assistant's updates. Switch it off there first: two would install the same updates.
error.invalid_operator_key: Not an Ed25519 public key in base64 (32 bytes), as `vordr-release public-key` prints it.
error.invalid_backup_operator_key: Not an Ed25519 public key in base64 (32 bytes), as `vordr-release public-key` prints it.
error.backup_without_operator_key: A backup key needs the operator key.
error.backup_equals_operator_key: The backup key is the same as the operator key.
error.ai_entity_missing: This entity does not exist or is unavailable.
error.ai_entity_unsupported: This entity cannot generate data, or AI Task is not set up.
error.ai_data_ack_missing: Confirm what goes to the provider, or leave the entity empty.

command_refused.message: {node}: the hub did not run the command ({code}).

refresh_dependencies_unsupported.message: {node}: the dependencies of {location} cannot be refreshed (so far only npm folders with a lock file, and an agent from 0.12.0 on).

update_image_not_allowed.message: {node}: {service} cannot be updated by button. The host's agent.yaml must allow it (image:{service} in install.allowed_scopes), and its image must carry a tag without a pinned digest and come from a registry.

command_refused_role_forbids.message: {node}: this Home Assistant may not start that - its role at the hub does not allow it (vordr-hub client-role).

command_refused_backup_stale.message: {node}: not installed - the last backup ({group}) is {age} h old, at most {max} h are allowed. Back up first, then install.

command_refused_backup_missing.message: {node}: not installed - PBS has no backup in {group}.

command_refused_backup_unreachable.message: {node}: not installed - Proxmox Backup Server does not answer, so the backup cannot be checked.

command_refused_backup_unmapped.message: {node}: not installed - hub.yaml names no PBS group for this host (backup.guests).

command_refused_backup_host_unknown.message: {node}: not installed - the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and the hub does not know that host. Check before_install in hub.yaml.

command_refused_backup_host_not_approved.message: {node}: not installed - the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent is not approved at the hub.

command_refused_backup_host_no_guest_bac.message: {node}: not installed - the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent makes no backups: its agent.yaml has no guest_backup, or the agent is too old.

command_refused_backup_host_offline.message: {node}: not installed - the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent is offline. Install again once it is back.

command_refused_backup_host_unavailable.message: {node}: not installed - the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent is not there (offline, not approved, or without guest_backup).

outside_window_unsupported.message: {node}: runs outside the window need a newer hub and agent. Update them first; until then the window holds.

outside_window_no_window.message: {node}: this has no window - use the normal button, it works at any time.

command_refused_outside_window.message: {node}: not installed - the host's window is closed, and its agent is too old to install outside it. Update the agent, or wait for the window.

command_refused_rate_limited.message: {node}: not installed - its last run was less than its minimum interval (install.min_interval_h) ago. Possible again from {next}.

reboot_window_closed.message: {node}: reboot only from {next} - the host's reboot window (reboot.window) is closed until then. To reboot now, use the action “Run outside the window” with a reason.

reboot_window_only.message: {node}: reboot only from {next} - the host's reboot window (reboot.window) is closed and does not open even with a reason (reboot.window_only).

confirm.title: Reboot {node} now?
confirm.description: Updates on {node} take full effect only after a reboot. Vördr asks the hub for the same reboot as the host's reboot button: the agent reboots only if it is still needed, and the host reports back once it is up again.

abort.hub_not_connected: Home Assistant is not connected to the Vördr hub right now. Try again once it is.
abort.reboot_not_offered: {node} no longer allows reboots through Vördr. Reboot it by hand.
abort.command_refused: The hub refused the reboot of {node} (code {code}).
abort.command_refused_role_forbids: The hub refused the reboot of {node}: this Home Assistant may not start it - its role at the hub does not allow it (vordr-hub client-role).
abort.reboot_window_closed: {node} can be rebooted only from {next}: its reboot window (reboot.window) is closed until then. Try again then, or reboot now with the action “Run outside the window” and a reason.
abort.reboot_window_only: {node} can be rebooted only from {next}: its reboot window (reboot.window) is closed and does not open even with a reason (reboot.window_only). Try again then.

reboot_required_manual.title: Vördr: {node} needs a reboot
reboot_required_manual.description: {node} has needed a reboot since {since}. This host does not allow reboots through Vördr: reboot it by hand. This notice goes away by itself once the host no longer needs a reboot.

confirm.title: Install again on {node}?
confirm.description: The last install on {node} failed: {code} ({detail}). Vördr keeps the failure as a problem until an install goes through. Once the cause is fixed, for example by hand, install again: Vördr asks the hub for the same install as the host's install button, also outside its window. If it goes through, the problem and this repair are gone, even when nothing is left to install; if the cause is still there, it fails again and both stay.

abort.hub_not_connected: Home Assistant is not connected to the Vördr hub right now. Try again once it is.
abort.no_longer_needed: {node} has no failed install any more.
abort.install_not_offered: {node} no longer allows installs through Vördr. Install by hand.
abort.command_refused: The hub refused the install on {node} (code {code}).
abort.command_refused_role_forbids: The hub refused the install on {node}: this Home Assistant may not start it - its role at the hub does not allow it (vordr-hub client-role).
abort.command_refused_outside_window: The hub refused the install on {node}: the host's window is closed, and its agent is too old to install outside it. Update the agent, or wait for the window.
abort.command_refused_rate_limited: The hub refused the install on {node}: its last run was less than its minimum interval (install.min_interval_h) ago. Possible again from {next}.
abort.command_refused_backup_stale: The hub refused the install on {node}: the last backup ({group}) is {age} h old, at most {max} h are allowed. Back up first, then install again.
abort.command_refused_backup_missing: The hub refused the install on {node}: PBS has no backup in {group}.
abort.command_refused_backup_unreachable: The hub refused the install on {node}: Proxmox Backup Server does not answer, so the backup cannot be checked.
abort.command_refused_backup_unmapped: The hub refused the install on {node}: hub.yaml names no PBS group for this host (backup.guests).
abort.command_refused_backup_host_unknown: The hub refused the install on {node}: the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and the hub does not know that host. Check before_install in hub.yaml.
abort.command_refused_backup_host_not_approved: The hub refused the install on {node}: the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent is not approved at the hub.
abort.command_refused_backup_host_no_guest_bac: The hub refused the install on {node}: the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent makes no backups: its agent.yaml has no guest_backup, or the agent is too old.
abort.command_refused_backup_host_offline: The hub refused the install on {node}: the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent is offline. Install again once it is back.
abort.command_refused_backup_host_unavailable: The hub refused the install on {node}: the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent is not there (offline, not approved, or without guest_backup).

problem_offline.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_offline.description:
Not connected to the hub for more than {offline_minutes} minutes.

Next step: Check the host and its agent.

problem_stale.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_stale.description:
Updates have been pending for more than {stale_days} days.

Next step: Install the updates, by hand or with the button.

problem_reboot_pending.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_reboot_pending.description:
A reboot has been needed for more than {reboot_days} days.

Next step: Reboot within the maintenance window.

problem_no_report.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_no_report.description:
Connected, but no check reported for more than {no_report_hours} hours.

Next step: Read the agent log.

problem_malicious_package.title: Vördr: malicious package on {node}
problem_malicious_package.description:
An installed package is known malware according to OSV: {packages}.

Next step: Remove the package and treat the host as compromised: renew the secrets it could reach, from another computer.

problem_vulnerable_package.title: Vördr: vulnerable package on {node}
problem_vulnerable_package.description:
Installed packages have known vulnerabilities according to OSV: {packages}.

Next step: Update the package to a fixed version.

problem_ok_reboot_required.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_ok_reboot_required.description:
OK, reboot required.

Next step: Reboot within the window or with the button.

problem_rejected_invalid_job.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_invalid_job.description:
Rejected: invalid job.

Next step: Check the hub and the clock – this may point to an attack.

problem_rejected_scope_not_allowed.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_scope_not_allowed.description:
Rejected: scope not allowed.

Next step: Check the host policy.

problem_rejected_outside_window.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_outside_window.description:
Rejected: outside the window.

Next step: Wait for the maintenance window, or start it outside the window with a reason (action “Install outside the window” or “Run outside the window”).

problem_rejected_rate_limited.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_rate_limited.description:
Rejected: too frequent.

Next step: Wait a few minutes.

problem_rejected_busy.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_busy.description:
Rejected: busy.

Next step: Try again later; stop other updaters running at the same time (e.g. unattended-upgrades).

problem_rejected_not_allowed.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_not_allowed.description:
Rejected: not allowed by the host.

Next step: Check the host policy.

problem_rejected_unsupported.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_unsupported.description:
Rejected: not supported.

Next step: Update the agent.

problem_rejected_not_idle.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_not_idle.description:
Rejected: the host is busy (idle check).

Next step: Wait until the host's own tasks are done (its idle check, reboot.idle_check), then reboot again.

problem_rejected_last_reboot_failed.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_rejected_last_reboot_failed.description:
Rejected: the last reboot did not take.

Next step: Reboot the host another way once and look why the last reboot did not help (e.g. which kernel the boot loader starts).

problem_precheck_disk_space.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_disk_space.description:
Not enough disk space.

Next step: Free up space (package cache, /boot).

problem_precheck_package_db_broken.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_package_db_broken.description:
Package database broken.

Next step: Run dpkg --configure -a on the host.

problem_precheck_repo_unreachable.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_repo_unreachable.description:
Package source unreachable.

Next step: Check the package source and the network.

problem_precheck_hash_mismatch.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_hash_mismatch.description:
Installer does not match its hash.

Next step: Wait for a corrected package manifest; if the publisher did not replace the file, check where it comes from.

problem_precheck_would_remove_packages.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_would_remove_packages.description:
Would remove packages.

Next step: Decide by hand: the update would remove packages.

problem_precheck_version_flagged.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_version_flagged.description:
Version flagged by OSV.

Next step: Look at the OSV entry and wait for a fixed version.

problem_precheck_version_too_new.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_version_too_new.description:
Version too new.

Next step: Wait until the release is old enough.

problem_precheck_vetting_unavailable.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_vetting_unavailable.description:
Hub could not check the plan.

Next step: Check the hub's vulnerability data.

problem_precheck_not_from_registry.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_precheck_not_from_registry.description:
Package not from the registry.

Next step: Look at where the dependency points; update such a location by hand.

problem_failed_package_manager.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_package_manager.description:
Package manager failed.

Next step: Read the excerpt of the last run.

problem_failed_verification.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_verification.description:
Verification failed.

Next step: Read the excerpt of the last run.

problem_failed_health.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_health.description:
Check after the update failed.

Next step: Look at the service named in the run.

problem_failed_windows_update.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_windows_update.description:
Windows Update failed.

Next step: Look up the HRESULT.

problem_failed_target_auth.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_target_auth.description:
Device login refused.

Next step: Check the device's service account and its password in the secret store.

problem_failed_target_tls.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_target_tls.description:
Device certificate does not match.

Next step: Check the device's certificate; if it changed on purpose, update the pinned fingerprint - otherwise someone may be in between.

problem_failed_target_hostkey.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_target_hostkey.description:
Device SSH host key does not match.

Next step: Check the device's SSH host key (ssh-keyscan); if it changed on purpose, update target.host_key - otherwise someone may be in between.

problem_failed_config_backup.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_config_backup.description:
Configuration backup failed.

Next step: Look at the proxy instance's log; without a fresh backup no firmware update starts.

problem_failed_backup.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_failed_backup.description:
Backup before the install failed.

Next step: Read the run's detail and the hypervisor's backup log; nothing was installed.

problem_timeout.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_timeout.description:
Timed out.

Next step: Check the host.

problem_aborted.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_aborted.description:
Aborted.

Next step: Start the run again if needed.

problem_interrupted.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_interrupted.description:
Interrupted.

Next step: Check the package database.

problem_unknown.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_unknown.description:
Unknown result code {code}.

Next step: Bring agent and hub to the same version.

problem_reboot_pending_manual.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_reboot_pending_manual.description:
A reboot has been needed for more than {reboot_days} days.

Next step: Reboot by hand - this host does not allow reboots through Vördr.

problem_ok_reboot_required_manual.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_ok_reboot_required_manual.description:
OK, reboot required.

Next step: Reboot by hand - this host does not allow reboots through Vördr.

problem_stale_manual.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_stale_manual.description:
Updates have been pending for more than {stale_days} days.

Next step: Install the updates by hand - this host does not allow installs through Vördr.

problem_stale_policy.title: Vördr: update problem on {node}
problem_stale_policy.description:
Updates have been pending for more than {stale_days} days. The host's policy lets Vördr install none of them: it allows only security updates and none of these is one, or its install mode holds them back.

Next step: Install them by hand, or widen the install section of the host's agent.yaml.

protocol_mismatch.title: Vördr: hub too old or too new
protocol_mismatch.description: The hub refuses this integration's protocol version {protocol}. Update the hub or the integration so that they match.

client_rejected.title: Vördr: the hub refuses this Home Assistant
client_rejected.description: The hub refuses the client {name} ({reason}). Check on the hub with `vordr-hub clients`; fingerprint of this client: `{fingerprint}`.

waiting_host.title: Vördr: host {node} waits for approval
waiting_host.description:
A host asks the hub to admit it as {node} (system `{os}`). The hub saw its key with this fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

Approval is at the hub: Home Assistant may approve hosts only where hub.yaml sets `ha_approves_hosts` and this client has role admin. If you expect this host, run `vordr-agent identity` on the host itself (for a device behind a proxy agent, with the `--config` of its instance) and compare. Only if both fingerprints are the same, run on the hub:

`{command}`

If they differ, do not approve: another key asks under this name, and `vordr-hub reject {node}` keeps it out. This hint goes away once the host is approved, rejected or forgotten.

confirm.title: Approve {node}?
confirm.description:
A host asks the hub to admit it as {node} (system `{os}`). The hub saw its key with this fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

If you expect this host, run `vordr-agent identity` on the host itself (for a device behind a proxy agent, with the `--config` of its instance) and enter the fingerprint it prints below - from the host, not from this text: only that comparison shows that the key is the host's. If both are the same, Home Assistant asks the hub to approve the host, and it shows as a device of this integration shortly. Instead, you can also run on the hub:

`{command}`

If they differ, do not approve: another key asks under this name, and `vordr-hub reject {node}` on the hub keeps it out. This repair goes away once the host is approved, rejected or forgotten.

data_description.fingerprint: As `vordr-agent identity` prints it on the host: 64 hex digits. Spaces and upper case do not matter.

error.invalid_fingerprint: That is no fingerprint: `vordr-agent identity` prints 64 hex digits (0-9, a-f).
error.fingerprint_differs: This is not the fingerprint the hub saw for this host. Do not approve it: another key asks under this name. Nothing was sent; keep it out at the hub with `vordr-hub reject` and the host's name, as shown above.

abort.hub_not_connected: Home Assistant is not connected to the Vördr hub right now. Try again once it is.
abort.no_longer_waiting: {node} no longer waits for approval: the hub approved, rejected or forgot it meanwhile.
abort.approval_not_offered: The hub no longer lets this Home Assistant approve hosts (hub.yaml `ha_approves_hosts`, role admin). Approve {node} at the hub with the command its repair shows.
abort.approve_ha_approval_off: The hub refused: it does not let Home Assistant approve hosts (`ha_approves_hosts` in hub.yaml is off). Approve {node} at the hub with the command its repair shows.
abort.approve_client_not_approved: The hub refused: it does not count this Home Assistant as an approved client (any more); `vordr-hub clients` at the hub tells. {node} still waits.
abort.approve_role_forbids: The hub refused: only a client with role admin may approve hosts, and this Home Assistant has another role (vordr-hub client-role). {node} still waits.
abort.approve_unknown_node: The hub refused: it does not know {node} (any more); it was forgotten meanwhile.
abort.approve_not_waiting: The hub refused: {node} no longer waits for approval, it was approved or rejected meanwhile. A rejection is undone only at the hub.
abort.approve_fingerprint_mismatch: The hub refused: {node} waits with another key than this fingerprint names. Do not approve it; check the host, and keep it out at the hub with `vordr-hub reject {node}` if in doubt.
abort.approve_bad_request: The hub refused the fingerprint as malformed. {node} still waits.
abort.approve_store_failed: The hub could not write its register, so {node} still waits. Check the hub's log and disk, then try again.
abort.approve_no_answer: The hub did not answer in time. Whether {node} was approved shows shortly: this repair goes away once it is.

confirm.title: Install {entity_id} again now?
confirm.description: Vördr's install of {entity_id} from {from_version} to {to_version} failed on {at}: Home Assistant or the entity's integration refused it or reported an error (see the log). Vördr does not try this version again by itself; a newer version is tried in its window. Once the cause is fixed, confirm here: Vördr installs it at once, outside the window but under all its other rules, with the backup before it where one is needed; if another install is running or a rule stops it, it says why and installs nothing. You can also install it by hand. This repair goes once an install of it goes through, and comes back if the next try fails.

abort.no_longer_needed: {entity_id} has no failed install any more.
abort.entry_not_loaded: The Vördr integration is not loaded right now. Try again once it is.
abort.busy: Another update is being installed right now, or Home Assistant is making a backup. Vördr installs one at a time and queues nothing: try again once it has finished.
abort.paused: Home Assistant updates are paused (switch "Pause Home Assistant updates"). Switch the pause off, then try again.
abort.auto_install_off: Installing Home Assistant updates is switched off in Vördr's options. Switch "Install automatically" on, or install {entity_id} by hand.
abort.other_entry: Another Vördr entry installs Home Assistant updates too, so neither does. Switch it off in one of them, then try again.
abort.backup_held: Home Assistant's last backup failed, and {entity_id} needs one before it is installed. Try again once Home Assistant shows a newer backup.
abort.not_ready: Vördr's rules do not let {entity_id} through now, apart from the window: the sensor "Updates ready" says why.

ha_updates_backup_failed.title: Vördr: Home Assistant's backup before an update failed
ha_updates_backup_failed.description: Before it installs an update that cannot back itself up, Vördr needs Home Assistant's automatic backup from the last 26 hours. On {at} there was none, and none could be made (see Settings, System, Backups, and the log). Until a newer automatic backup shows up, Vördr installs only updates that make their own backup, and it tries to make one again after 24 hours. This notice goes away once Home Assistant has a newer automatic backup.

common.same_major: or {tag} in the same major version
common.images_report_only: Only reported, Vördr does not update images:

update_package.name: Update a package
update_package.description: Updates one pip or npm package of a location to its candidate (public for at least the host's minimum age, checked against OSV by the hub).

package.name: Package
package.description: Name of the package, as the location lists it.

reason.name: Reason (outside the window)
reason.description: Optional: why now, outside the host's maintenance window. Without one, the hub notes that it was started in Home Assistant. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

refresh_dependencies.name: Refresh dependencies
refresh_dependencies.description: Moves the dependencies of a location that have findings to the newest release their dependents allow (public for at least the host's minimum age, checked against OSV by the hub). A dependency that no allowed release fixes stays as it is; the run says why.

reason.name: Reason (outside the window)
reason.description: Optional: why now, outside the host's maintenance window. Without one, the hub notes that it was started in Home Assistant. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

install_outside_window.name: Install outside the window
install_outside_window.description: Installs like the install button of a Vördr update entity (system packages, a pip/npm location or container images), with a reason of your own. The install button itself also runs outside the host's maintenance window; this action says why. Automatic runs keep to the window.

reason.name: Reason
reason.description: Why now, at most 200 bytes. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

press_outside_window.name: Run outside the window
press_outside_window.description: Presses a Vördr button (install security updates, install an app, reboot) with a reason of your own. A reboot outside the host's window needs it, unless the host keeps its reboot window shut even for a reason (reboot.window_only); the install buttons run outside the window anyway. Rebooting still needs the admin role at the hub.

reason.name: Reason
reason.description: Why now, at most 200 bytes. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

update_image.name: Update a container image
update_image.description: Moves one Compose service to the rebuild of its tag, once that build is at least the host's minimum age old. The running image stays on the host as the way back: if the service does not come back healthy, the agent returns to it. A newer tag needs the Compose file changed and stays manual.

service.name: Service
service.description: The Compose service as PROJECT/SERVICE, as the entity's attribute updates lists it under services.

reason.name: Reason (outside the window)
reason.description: Optional: why now, outside the host's maintenance window. Without one, the hub notes that it was started in Home Assistant. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

options.firmware: Device firmware (Zigbee, Matter, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi devices and others)
